sections.label: Denying input GST claims
sections.summary: The Comptroller of GST may deny a GST-registered business's input GST claim if the business knew or should have known its purchase was part of a fraudulent arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The first measure allows the Comptroller of GST to deny a GST-registered business’ input GST claim, if the business knew or should have known that his purchase was part of a fraudulent arrangement.

sections.label: Surcharge on denied input GST
sections.summary: A 10% surcharge applies on the amount of input GST denied for a GST-registered business that should have known its purchase was part of a fraudulent arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The second measure introduces a surcharge of 10% to be applied on the amount of input GST denied for a GST-registered business which should have known that its purchase was part of a fraudulent arrangement.

sections.label: Conditions on GST registration
sections.summary: The Comptroller may impose conditions on a business required to register for GST.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The third measure allows the Comptroller to impose conditions on a business which is required to register for GST.

sections.label: Removing Comptroller's tax avoidance discretion
sections.summary: The first amendment removes the Comptroller of GST's discretion to disregard or vary arrangements carried out with tax avoidance as a main purpose and not for bona fide commercial reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Under the first amendment, we will remove the discretion for the Comptroller of GST to disregard or vary arrangements that are carried out with tax avoidance as one of their main purposes, and not for bona fide commercial reasons.

sections.label: Surcharge on tax avoidance adjustments
sections.summary: The second amendment introduces a surcharge equal to 50% of additional GST payable from the Comptroller's adjustments to counteract tax avoidance arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The second amendment further deters tax avoidance arrangements, by introducing a surcharge equal to 50% of the amount of additional GST payable as a result of the adjustments made by the Comptroller to counteract tax avoidance arrangements.

sections.label: Time limit for GST refund claims
sections.summary: Claims for overpaid or erroneously paid GST must be made to IRAS within five years, and apply also to GST on imported goods.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The amendments clarify that such claims relating to overpaid or erroneously paid GST must be made to IRAS within five years from the end of the relevant GST accounting period or the date on which the GST was paid; and that such claims are also applicable to overpaid or erroneously paid GST on imported goods.

sections.label: Electronic GST refunds via subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: MOF may prescribe in subsidiary legislation that the Comptroller of GST refunds GST to GST-registered businesses electronically.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: MOF will be allowed to prescribe in subsidiary legislation that refunds of GST are to be made by the Comptroller of GST to GST-registered businesses via electronic means.

sections.label: Comptroller disclosing information to IRAS CEO
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Comptroller of GST disclose information to the IRAS CEO or authorised officers and let them access records for their duties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The amendment allows the Comptroller of GST to disclose information to the CEO of IRAS, or officers authorised by the CEO of IRAS for that purpose and allow these officers to access any records or documents where necessary for the purpose of these duties.

sections.label: GST revenue figures and revised estimates
sections.summary: GST contributed $11.2 billion in FY 2019, and FY 2020 GST revenue was revised from $11.27 billion to $9.69 billion, a 14% reduction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In the context of Singapore, the GST is now one of the largest contributors to our operating revenues at $11.2 billion in FY 2019, behind corporate income tax at $16.8 billion and personal income tax at $12.2 billion respectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While GST revenues were initially estimated at $11.27 in FY 2020, this has since been revised to $9.69 billion or a 14% reduction given the impact of the current economic slowdown.

sections.label: Assessment of Missing Trader Fraud losses
sections.summary: The question asks for the Ministry's assessment of estimated annual losses in Singapore due to Missing Trader Fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To this end, I would like to ask what is the Ministry's assessment of the estimated annual losses in Singapore due to Missing Trader Fraud.

sections.label: COVID-19 impact on Singapore retail sector
sections.summary: COVID-19 accelerated e-commerce growth, with online sales at 10.9% in August and a high of 24.5% in May, while bricks-and-mortar retailers struggled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, COVID-19 has resulted in the dual impact to the retail sector in Singapore: first, an acceleration in the already rapid growth of the e-commerce market where online sales represented 10.9% of the latest retail sales value in August, having reached a high of 24.5% in May this year; secondly, the continued struggle of bricks-and-mortar retailers amid an uneven playing field.

sections.label: Bill draws on UK and Australia provisions
sections.summary: The Bill draws lessons from similar provisions in the UK and Australia and aims to improve GST administration and counter GST fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In doing so, this Bill draws lessons and references from similar provisions in other jurisdictions, such as the UK and Australia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I support this Bill, which will improve GST administration and enhance the Comptroller’s powers to safeguard public monies, investigate tax offences and counter GST fraud.

sections.label: Section 20 due diligence checks
sections.summary: Amendments to section 20 require businesses to do due diligence checks to avoid involvement in fraud they should have known.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments to section 20 require businesses to undertake due diligence checks to avoid being involved in a fraud that they “should have known”.

sections.label: Tips detect fraud most
sections.summary: The 2018 ACFE report found tips are the most common fraud detection method, with fifty percent of cases detected through tips.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Association of Certified Fraud Examiners 2018 report revealed that tips are consistently and, by far, the most common detection method for fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Fifty percent of the cases are detected through tips.

sections.label: Missing trader fraud GST figures
sections.summary: As at 31 December 2019, over 300 audited GST-registered businesses were suspected in missing trader fraud, with about $450 million GST involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As at 31 December 2019, more than 300 GST-registered businesses audited have been suspected to be involved in missing trader fraud in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The total GST involved is about $450 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Now, of these 300 GST-registered businesses, IRAS has completed its audit and investigation for about 70 businesses and the GST involved amongst these businesses is about $90 million in GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, the GST at risk of loss for this category is the remaining, that is, $450 million minus $90 million, so, it is $360 million.

sections.label: Comptroller bears burden of proof
sections.summary: Under the proposed arrangement, the Comptroller bears the burden of proving the business knew or should have known of the fraud.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under the proposed arrangement, the burden of proving that the GST-registered business knew or should have known of the fraudulent arrangement lies on the Comptroller, based on the balance of probabilities.

sections.label: Records of due diligence steps
sections.summary: Businesses should generally keep records of steps taken to ascertain whether a supply was likely part of a fraudulent arrangement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Business should, generally, maintain records of the steps taken to ascertain whether the supply made to or by the business was likely to be a part of a fraudulent arrangement and this includes documents detailing the risks assessed, the due diligence checks that were performed and the actions and precautions taken in response to the results surfacing from these checks.

sections.label: Five-year record retention period
sections.summary: Under the GST Act, GST-registered businesses must keep records for five years from the end of their prescribed accounting periods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the duration of how long the record should be maintained, under the GST Act, GST-registered businesses are required to keep the records for a period of five years from the end of their prescribed accounting periods.

sections.label: IRAS tax evasion whistleblowing
sections.summary: IRAS treats tax evasion reports seriously, allows direct reporting on IRAS officers or vendor staff, and keeps whistleblower identity and information confidential.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: IRAS takes every report of tax evasion seriously, and if the whistleblowing relates to an IRAS officer or a staff of IRAS' vendors, the whistleblower can write directly to the Director of IRAS' internal audit branch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We wish to assure Mr Ng that the whistleblower's identity and all information and documents provided would be kept confidential and subject to an independent evaluation within IRAS.
